items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: I think that's when Ken Kersey left the band... Bud Powell taken Ken Kersey's place... Ken Kersey was all right.

ctx.x: Oh, no. We hadn't been there... We weren't there all that time. No, we only played there a few weeks, I don't know how many weeks, and then we came out of there and we came back to the Savoy. See, we had come back to New York to the Savoy -- in New York here. And I think that's when Ken Kersey left the band... But see, they was always getting changes in the band. And I think Jonas Walker left the band. And of course, Bud Powell taken Ken Kersey's place. I don't know if he taken Ken Kersey's place or not, but...…

But Bud was the greatest of them all, Bud Powell -- and he was a genius. He was really a genius. He was about 17 years old when he come into Cootie's band. And he was a kid, and we was sittin' up there rehearsing. So Cootie's rehearsing this theme song for Bud; you know, so Bud can see how it goes.

items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: Yeah, I think Kenny Kersey did open the band... But anyway, Ken Kersey was all right.

ctx.x: Yeah, there was Louis Bacon, trumpet. He was from Russell's band, too! Also Chick Webb's band he was from. And he was also the vocalist in Cootie's band. He had a wonderful bass voice. Wonderful.

Then on the younger side, we had men like...I think it was Kenny Kersey; and Milton Fletcher on trumpet; and Joe Guy; Eddie Vinson... Well, Bob Dorsey, I would put him with the younger boys, because he was a nut. He was a real nut. In fact, all of the young ones, they were nuts. Believe me. They didn't care about anything. But they could play.

Oh, Kenny Kersey wasn't there. Or was he? Yeah, I guess Kenny Kersey did open the band. I really don't know who opened... Yeah, he opened up the band. Yeah, I think Kenny Kersey did open the band, because (?)Rich Carter(?) came along later, when we went into the Savoy... Bud Powell. Bud Powell came along later. But anyway, Ken Kersey was all right. He didn't bother nobody.
